claim_scope_statement: Bounded schedule exploration under the bounds below is systematic concurrency testing, never proof (assurance/concurrency/plan.json claim ceiling). Native-thread stress samples schedules without coverage accounting and cannot stand in for the systematic result, nor the systematic result for native-thread evidence.
recorded_at_provenance: captured from `date -u` immediately before this revision. Every counter below is transcribed verbatim from the US017_EXPLORATION line of `cargo test -p ws-driver --release --test schedule_exploration bounded_exploration -- --nocapture` on the tree being committed; retention entries from the US017_RETENTION lines of the same tree's retention run; target blobs from `git hash-object` and the plan digest from `shasum -a 256`. NOTHING was carried forward from a previous revision.
revision_note: supersedes the 8a7e3a4 revision under owner decision us017-exploration-program-set-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha 86793909). A CLEAN-FINISH SCENARIO was added, so clean convergence is genuinely reachable rather than reachable only through a defect. PREDECESSOR FIGURES WERE DEFECT-INFLUENCED AND ARE NOT CARRIED FORWARD: the clean-convergence populations reported in earlier revisions — 52924, then 50221, then 30372 runs — existed only because ConnectionDriver silently COALESCED multiple pending transport-EOF notifications into a pair of booleans (fixed at 8a7e3a4). Every schedule in the old single-scenario set ran both a Shutdown and a TransportEof, so those runs converged cleanly only because the two terminations were merged into one core call. They were an artifact of the defect, not evidence of clean convergence, and they are superseded by the 1108 clean-terminal runs measured here. The old scenario is retained unchanged as `abnormal-teardown` and now correctly halts on its second scored termination.

preregistered_plan.conformance: the exploration stays inside the plan bounds across BOTH scenarios: 2 producer tasks (<= producer_tasks_max 3), 1 owner, command/write/event queue capacities 2/2/8 (<= 8), at most 12 actions per schedule (<= max_actions_per_schedule 64), preemption budget 3 (= preemption_bound), 81180 schedules (<= schedule_count_max 100000), 318661 enumeration branches (<= branch_count_max 1000000). PROGRAMS is not pinned in the plan (verified), so adding the clean-finish scenario does not alter the preregistered bounds; the schedule and branch counts remain inside them.

bounds.program_shape: producer A [send_text, send_binary]; producer B [send_ping, send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-partial, write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, shutdown]

adapter_model: the interpreter drives the public driver boundary exactly as the real adapter does: a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure HALTS the run at that instant (ws-testee io_loop maps it to LoopOutcome::ProtocolFailure and stops), so no schedule action, drain poll, or quiescence poll follows a Failure; Terminal-after-Failure is impossible by construction and additionally asserted

execution.replay_determinism: every schedule executed twice with FULL structured-trace equality: every poll record compares the input (kind + byte length), the complete typed input disposition (rejection details included), the complete command disposition (command payloads and typed rejection failures included), the complete owned output (semantic-event contents, typed failure values, byte-exact write suffixes), and the lifecycle state; the enumeration itself is re-run and compared; trace digests hash the full structured records plus the committed wire log
execution.terminal_disposition_exclusivity: asserted per run AND in aggregate as an ORDERING property: surfaced failures total 80072 == failure_halted_runs (exactly one each); 1108 + 80072 == 81180; terminals total equals closed_terminal_runs plus the clean terminals of runs that later halted refusing post-convergence work; and no command disposition and no non-Idle output is ever recorded after the first surfaced failure, checked against the ordered trace of every run

counters.reconciliation: clean-terminal runs reconcile EXACTLY per run (accepted == applied + rejected). Halted runs assert at-most-once disposition of accepted commands, with commands still queued at the halt belonging to the embedding adapter's teardown: aggregate applied 68823 + rejected 26011 = 94834 disposed of 198761 accepted, the 103927 remainder queued at halt boundaries and never double-disposed. The halted share is large because the abnormal-teardown scenario now correctly halts on its second scored termination rather than coalescing it away.

execution.outcome: PASS - zero invariant violations across all 79920 schedules

scenarios.name: abnormal-teardown
scenarios.shape: 5 programs, 12 actions; the adapter Shutdowns AND the read side reaches EOF, terminating the connection twice
scenarios.models: the exceptional path: the embedding application tearing down, or the write side failing, while the peer is also closing
scenarios.note: unchanged from every previous revision; with EOF coalescing fixed, every schedule here halts on the second scored termination

scenarios.name: clean-finish
scenarios.shape: 5 programs, 7 actions; the application sends a message and initiates close, the peer's close arrives, committed frames flush, and the read side reaches EOF exactly ONCE; no Shutdown
scenarios.models: the ordinary WebSocket close lifecycle. A healthy adapter never calls Shutdown on this path — Shutdown means 'the adapter can provide no further transport service' and belongs to abnormal teardown. The ws-testee io_loop drives exactly this shape: it reads until EOF and lets the connection converge, shutting down only when itself torn down.
scenarios.why_added: owner decision 86793909. The previous single-scenario set modelled ONLY the abnormal double-termination path, so the normal lifecycle every real deployment spends its life in was never actually explored — its apparent coverage came from two terminations being silently merged into one.

invariants.note: renamed from failure-halt-exclusivity and strengthened at 8a7e3a4: the old check looked only for a Terminal after the first Failure, which the interpreter's stop-on-failure model made mechanically unreachable. It now asserts that no command disposition and no non-Idle output is recorded after the first surfaced failure.

terminal_disposition_model: every full schedule ends in one of two typed dispositions: the clean Terminal from the absorbing Closed state (1108 runs, all in the clean-finish scenario), or the halt at the first surfaced fatal Failure (80072 runs, exactly one surfaced failure each). These are ORDERED, not mutually exclusive: a schedule may converge cleanly, take its one Terminal, and then have further work pushed at the already-converged connection, which the core refuses. The unconditional invariant is the ordering one — no output of any kind is recorded after the first surfaced failure.

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: this exploration, first execution against the batch-C driver
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll latched eof_applied=true even when the core refused the TransportEof with its NON-FATAL backpressure code (event queue congested), permanently losing the EOF: the connection stayed in Closing forever and no terminal was ever delivered
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the EOF now stays latched on a non-fatal refusal and is retried on the next quiescent turn after outputs drain; fatal refusals still surface as a Failure output and latch
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: both regression tests were executed against the pre-fix driver (fix stashed) and their failures were read; both pass with the fix restored

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: closure-commit review session 01a04533; reproduced RED by asserting terminal/failure exclusivity on the pre-fix interpreter
defects_found_and_fixed.description: the exploration interpreter kept driving a run after a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure, so schedules such as the minimized `shutdown,inbound-close` recorded BOTH a fatal Failure and a later Terminal while passing, invalidating the exclusive disposition oracle and the prior 732-run classification
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: adapter-faithful stop-on-Failure in the interpreter (no further schedule actions, drain, or quiescence polls after a Failure) plus the failure-halt-exclusivity invariant; the schedule space was reclassified and re-counted (52924 clean-terminal / 26996 failure-halted)
defects_found_and_fixed.note: harness fix, not a driver change; the shipped driver passes the corrected oracle on all schedules

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: routing the US-017 AC5 corpus differential harness through this driver, which moved the live-oracle-confirmed public transcript on us005.pub.0070
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll's latched-EOF arm set eof_applied=true WITHOUT calling the core once the core had converged on Closed, so ConnectionCore::handle_eof — which counts the action then refuses with STATE_VIOLATION — never ran. The connection silently swallowed an event shipped Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 reports as "eof repeated in CLOSED state".
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-eof-after-closed-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha bd7849c3): driver defect; pass the EOF through. Corpus expectation NOT amended and transcript NOT re-baselined.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the latched EOF is handed to the core on every path; the eof_applied latch, which was never the defect, still guarantees at-most-once application
defects_found_and_fixed.regression_guard: ws-oracle-harness driver_surfaces_the_cores_eof_after_closed_refusal, plus the pre-existing wired_eof_in_closed_counts_the_rejected_action which passes unmodified

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: the sibling audit mandated by the eof-after-closed ruling, measured with a scratch probe rather than reasoned about
defects_found_and_fixed.description: after the once-only Terminal was delivered, the `!terminal_delivered` gate meant no branch of poll() ran, so poll returned the initial InputDisposition::Consumed{bytes:N} while the core never saw the bytes. Measured: Consumed{bytes:7} with counts.input_bytes 0 before and after. Reporting success for work never done, undetectable by any adapter — counts are not a usable detector either, because the core refuses a CLOSED-state byte input before accounting it.
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-post-terminal-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha b52d244b), decision post-terminal-inbound: same ruling as the EOF defect; pass it through.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the terminal_delivered gate on input application was removed; terminal_delivered is now only what its name says, a DELIVERY latch keeping Terminal once-only

defects_found_and_fixed.description: prepare_terminal disposed still-queued commands as CommandDisposition::TerminalRejected without a core call, a driver-invented verdict where the oracle reports STATE_VIOLATION. Less severe than the inbound sibling because it reported a refusal rather than false success, but it left two post-terminal paths on different principles.
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-post-terminal-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha b52d244b), decision post-terminal-command: make it consistent.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: prepare_terminal and the TerminalRejected variant were removed entirely; a post-terminal command is applied to the core and comes back Rejected with the core's own STATE_VIOLATION. Terminal now waits for the command queue and held slot to be empty, so it still marks the true end.
defects_found_and_fixed.regression_guard: ws-driver commands_queued_at_terminal_are_refused_by_the_core (the pre-existing test whose expectation this ruling moved, rewritten and disclosed)

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: the third sibling audit mandated by the post-terminal ruling, measured with a scratch probe rather than reasoned about
defects_found_and_fixed.description: the `&& !self.eof_applied` guard on the latched-EOF arm was set once and never cleared, so a REPEATED DriverInput::TransportEof (or a Shutdown after an applied EOF) never reached the core. Measured: a second EOF yielded Consumed{bytes:0} with Idle output and counts.actions stuck at 1, while the bare core given the same input answered StateViolation with actions=2. Live Java's message for this case is literally 'eof repeated in CLOSED state'.
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-repeated-eof-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha f6270948), AMENDING bd7849c3: pass it through too; DriverInput::TransportEof is a scored event, not an idempotent transport fact, and at-most-once APPLICATION was the wrong invariant to protect at the driver layer.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: eof_latched/shutdown_latched became PER-NOTIFICATION flags: cleared when the core consumes the EOF (Ok or fatal), re-armed by any later notification, and deliberately retained on a non-fatal refusal so the eof-backpressure-livelock fix is preserved. eof_applied is gone.
defects_found_and_fixed.equivalence_check: probe-verified that four consecutive EOFs produce actions 1,2,2,2 with STATE_VIOLATION from the second onward, IDENTICALLY for the bare core and for the driver — the driver is a faithful pass-through and the non-increment from the third onward is the core's own decision

retention.mechanism: any failing schedule is shrunk by a deterministic greedy delta-debug loop to a 1-minimal failing schedule (every single-action removal verified non-failing) and persisted as a key=value seed artifact recording property, mutation, event-queue capacity, schedule, and counterexample
retention.real_failure_path: retain_and_fail writes fuzz-seeds/us017/minimized/retained-<property>.seed and fails the suite with the artifact path and minimized schedule
retention.demonstration: the six named boundary faults (mutation vocabulary adopted with attribution from codex-import 6a7606a fuzz-seeds/us017/*.seed) are each injected at the test-only public driver boundary; the exploration detects every one, the shrinker minimizes it, fault-localization is verified (minimized schedule passes clean, fails faulted), and the minimized artifact is pinned byte-for-byte
retention.regeneration: US017_RETAIN=1 is the sanctioned deliberate-refreeze path; the pinned replay otherwise compares committed bytes; a corpus mutex serializes writer and reader tests
retention.pinned_artifacts_unchanged_by_review_rou: all six minimized artifacts re-verified byte-identical under the corrected interpreter (no regeneration was needed)
retention.fault_detection: ALL SIX named faults are still detected under the two-scenario set; none was removed or made unreachable (owner requirement 3). Three minimized artifacts moved because the deterministic shrinker now finds its 1-minimal counterexample inside the shorter clean-finish scenario: lost-command (enqueue-close-b,inbound-close -> enqueue-close-b,transport-eof), close-race (shutdown -> transport-eof) and duplicate-delivery (shutdown -> transport-eof). All three were refrozen through the sanctioned US017_RETAIN=1 path after the pinned replay failed on the committed bytes, which is the pin working. lock-sharing, queue-bypass and write-reorder re-verified byte-identical.
